# OHZI Core — Instructions for Large Language Models

> OHZI Core (`ohzi-core` on npm) is a TypeScript graphics library built on top of Three.js.
> It provides a structured application lifecycle, scene management, asset loading,
> shader materials, post-processing, and rendering pipelines for WebGL/WebGPU projects.
> It is not standalone — it is designed to be used within the OHZI Boilerplate project.

## Project Identity

- **Name:** ohzi-core
- **Author:** OHZI Interactive Studio
- **License:** MIT
- **Language:** TypeScript (ES Modules)
- **Runtime dependency:** Three.js (0.183.0)
- **Renderer target:** Three.js WebGPU renderer
- **Repository:** https://github.com/ohzinteractive/core
- **Companion project:** https://github.com/ohzinteractive/boilerplate

## What This Library Does

OHZI Core gives you:

1. **A frame loop with lifecycle hooks** — Extend `BaseApplication` and override methods like `update()`, `on_pre_render()`, `fixed_update()`, etc. The `RenderLoop` class drives everything.
2. **A managed rendering pipeline** — `Graphics` wraps the Three.js renderer. Swap between render modes (Normal, Unreal Bloom, Normal+AO, Deferred, VR, Debug Normals) at runtime.
3. **Scene management with progressive loading** — `AbstractScene` provides a two-phase asset loading pipeline (regular + high-quality) with compilators that spread GPU upload work across frames.
4. **30+ custom shader materials** — SSAO, bloom, Gaussian blur, dual-filter blur, FXAA, deferred rendering, SDF text, depth/normal passes, and more.
5. **Asset loading** — 17 individual loaders (GLTF, DRACO, textures, HDR, cubemaps, audio, fonts, video, OBJ, DAE, etc.) plus async batch loaders. `ResourceContainer` deduplicates by URL.
6. **Post-processing utilities** — Gaussian blur, dual-filtering blur, depth/normals renderer, blitter, material passes.
7. **Camera controller** — Pluggable movement modes and states for interactive camera control.
8. **View/UI layer** — `ViewManager`, `ViewComponent`, and `TransitionManager` for application state and animated transitions.
9. **Utilities** — Math helpers (`OMath`), easing functions, geometry utilities, camera fitting, mesh sampling, raycasting, SDF text rendering, canvas drawing, CSS animation, and more.

## Architecture Overview

### Core Singletons

These are instantiated once at module level and exported by name. `Initializer.init()` initializes all of them except `Graphics`, which needs its own `Graphics.init()`:

| Singleton | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Graphics` | Wraps Three.js renderer; manages render modes, blitting, screenshots |
| `Time` | `delta_time`, `smooth_delta_time`, `elapsed_time`, fixed timestep (1/30) |
| `OScreen` | Viewport dimensions (logical and physical), DPR, aspect ratio, resize detection |
| `SceneManager` | Holds and disposes the active `AbstractScene` |
| `CameraManager` | Global access to the active camera (and VR spectator camera) |
| `Debug` | Debug visualization layer (3D shapes, textures, 2D overlays) |
| `ResourceContainer` | Asset cache keyed by name and URL |
| `OS` | Platform detection (mobile, iOS, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux) |
| `Browser` | Browser detection |
| `Capabilities` | GPU/feature capability detection |

### Frame Lifecycle

`RenderLoop` calls these hooks each frame in order:

```
Time.__update()
on_post_start()        ← second frame only
input.update()
before_update()
TransitionManager.before_update()
fixed_update()         ← runs in a loop at fixed 1/30s timestep, each step followed by TransitionManager.fixed_update()
update()
TransitionManager.update()
ViewManager.update()
ViewComponentManager.update()
on_pre_render()
Graphics.update()      ← renders the scene via the active render mode
on_post_render()
Debug.render()
on_frame_end()
```

Users implement these by extending `BaseApplication`:

```typescript
import { BaseApplication, RenderLoop, Graphics, Initializer } from 'ohzi-core';

class MyApp extends BaseApplication {
  on_enter(loop: RenderLoop) { /* setup */ }
  update()                   { /* per-frame logic */ }
  on_pre_render()            { /* before render */ }
  on_post_render()           { /* after render */ }
  fixed_update()             { /* physics at 1/30 */ }
  on_exit(loop: RenderLoop)  { /* cleanup */ }
}
```

### Initialization Sequence

```typescript
import { Initializer, Graphics, RenderLoop } from 'ohzi-core';

// 1. Initialize core singletons
Initializer.init(input);

// 2. Initialize graphics (requires a renderer instance)
Graphics.init({ renderer, core_attributes: { xr_enabled: false }, dpr });

// 3. Create and start the render loop
const app = new MyApp();
const loop = new RenderLoop(app, Graphics, input);
loop.start();
```

### Rendering Pipeline

`Graphics` supports multiple render modes via `Graphics.set_state()`, which calls `on_exit()` on the old mode and `on_enter()` on the new one:

| Render Mode | Description |
|---|---|
| `NormalRender` | Standard forward rendering |
| `UnrealBloomRender` | Forward rendering with Unreal-style bloom: five Gaussian blur mips, an optional luminosity high pass, and per-mip tints. `new UnrealBloomRender(use_antialiasing, use_half_float, use_hight_luminosity_pass, use_rendering_size = false)`: the first three are required |
| `NormalAORender` | Forward rendering with SSAO. `new NormalAORender(use_ssaa = false, use_exact_depth = true)`: turning `use_exact_depth` off roughly halves the SSAO pass cost but bands flat surfaces |
| `BloomRender` | Basic bloom rendering. `new BloomRender(true)` blurs with `DualFilteringBlurrer` instead of the box blur, for a much wider glow |
| `DeferredRender` | Deferred point lights over the depth and normals buffer. Starts with a 2×2 grid of demo lights in `scene_lights` |
| `VRRender` | For WebXR (`xr_enabled`). Three's XR manager renders the stereo views; the mode mirrors the headset view to the canvas through `CameraManager.spectator` |
| `DebugNormalsRender` | Visualizes world-space surface normals |

All render modes extend `BaseRender` and implement a `render()` method called by `Graphics.update()`. Only `NormalRender` and `VRRender` call the scene's `on_pre_render()`, `render()` and `on_post_render()` hooks; the others render `SceneManager.current` directly. `NormalAORender` and `DeferredRender` turn on `Graphics.generate_depth_normal_texture` and never turn it off.

`BloomRender`, `UnrealBloomRender`, `NormalAORender`, `DeferredRender` and `DebugNormalsRender` use TSL materials and run on `WebGPURenderer` with both its WebGPU and WebGL2 backends.

### Scene & Asset Loading

`AbstractScene` extends Three.js `Scene` with a two-phase loading pipeline:

```
load() → init() → RegularLoadingState → on_assets_ready() → compilators → on_assets_compiled()
                 → HighQualityLoadingState → on_high_quality_assets_ready()
```

Individual asset loaders (all in `src/resource_loader/`):

| Loader | Formats |
|---|---|
| `GLTFLoader` | .gltf, .glb |
| `GLTFDRACOLoader` | DRACO-compressed GLTF |
| `TextureLoader` | .png, .jpg, .webp, etc. |
| `AsyncTextureLoader` | Images through `createImageBitmap` (`Image` on Safari) |
| `HDRTextureLoader` | .hdr |
| `HDRCubeTextureLoader` | HDR cubemaps |
| `CubemapLoader` | Standard cubemaps |
| `BasisLoader` | Basis Universal textures |
| `AudioLoader` | Audio files |
| `VideoLoader` | Video files |
| `FontLoader` | three.js typeface JSON fonts |
| `OBJLoader` | .obj |
| `DAELoader` | .dae (Collada) |
| `JSONLoader` | JSON data |
| `FileLoader` | Raw files |
| `TextLoader` | Text files |
| `PointArrayLoader` | Newline separated x, y, z values → `Vector3[]` |

Batch loaders (`AsyncTexturesLoader`, `AsyncObjectsLoader`, `AsyncAudiosLoader`) handle groups of assets. `ResourceContainer` reuses a resource already stored for the same URL, but two loads of one URL that start before either finishes both download.

Each loader is built with `(resource_id, url, ..., size)` and `load(resource_container)` returns nothing: poll `has_finished` / `has_error`. `ResourceBatch` runs a group of loaders on the main thread (`add_loader`, `load`, `loading_finished`, `get_progress`). The async loaders extend `AsyncAbstractLoader`: a shared worker (`AsyncAbstractLoader.create_worker()`, stored as `ResourceContainer` `'assets_worker'`) downloads each asset into a blob URL, and the main thread decodes it.

### Shader Materials

Every custom material is TSL and runs on `WebGPURenderer` with both the WebGPU and WebGL2 backends. There is no GLSL in core. Materials extend `BlitNodeMaterial` (a `NodeMaterial`) or `NodeMaterial` and keep the `uniforms.<name>.value` contract; these include `SSAOMaterial`, `SSAOComposeMaterial`, `BoxBlurMaterial`, `GaussianBlurMaterial`, `LuminosityHighPassMaterial`, `UnrealBloomComposeMaterial`, `DepthNormalMaterial`, `AddMaterial`, `ScreenSpaceTextureMaterial` (behind `Debug.draw_texture`), `WorldImageMaterial` (behind `WorldImage` and `Text2D`), `LineMaterial` (behind `Line`), `SDFTextMaterial` (behind `SDFTextBatch`) and `DualFilteringBlurMaterial` (behind `DualFilteringBlurrer`). `Debug.draw_plane` and `draw_math_sphere` use `MeshBasicNodeMaterial`, so every `Debug` helper runs on `WebGPURenderer`.

Key materials: `SSAOMaterial`, `SSAOComposeMaterial`, `GaussianBlurMaterial`, `DualFilteringBlurMaterial`, `LuminosityHighPassMaterial`, `UnrealBloomComposeMaterial`, `DepthNormalMaterial`, `SDFTextMaterial`, `BlitNodeMaterial`, `AddMaterial`.

### Post-Processing Utilities

| Utility | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GaussianBlurrer` | Multi-pass Gaussian blur on render targets. `blur(RT, use_luminosity_high_pass)` leaves `RT` unchanged and writes five mips, each at half the previous size, to `renderTargetsVertical`. Behind `UnrealBloomRender` |
| `DualFilteringBlurrer` | Kawase dual-filter blur (faster, lower quality). `blur(render_target)` blurs in place, down to a sixteenth of the input and back. Its taps rely on linear filtering, which render targets have by default. Runs on `WebGPURenderer` |
| `Blurrer` | 9 tap separable blur at the input's size. `blur(render_target)` blurs in place |
| `DepthAndNormalsRenderer` | Generates depth/normal textures for SSAO and effects |
| `Blitter` | Copies render targets with optional material passes |

Post-processing materials: `BlitNodeMaterial` (base of every full screen pass; `Graphics.blit()` sets its `_MainTex`, `_Resolution` and `_TargetResolution`), `AddMaterial` (`_MainTex + _SecondTex`), `UnrealBloomComposeMaterial` (sums tinted blur mips; run with `Graphics.material_pass()`) and `DualFilteringBlurMaterial`.

### Components

Renderable components in `src/components/`:

| Component | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Grid` | Debug grid: a 100 × 100 unit plane on XZ with a line every unit |
| `Line` | Thick polyline drawn as a ribbon that faces the camera (`thickness`, `color`). `setup(points)` rebuilds it with 2 or more points; a new point count replaces `geometry`. Runs on `WebGPURenderer` |
| `Text2D` | Text drawn on a canvas and shown as a `WorldImage`, in its CSS fill color. Setting `text` redraws it; the plane is 1 unit tall at any font size |
| `SDFTextBatch` | Multi channel SDF text, every text it holds in one instanced draw (`add_text`, `remove_text`, `set_boldness`; call `update()` every frame). Atlas bounds count from the bottom (`yOrigin: bottom`). The batch transform is ignored; place each text with its `set_position`/`set_size`/`set_rotation`. Runs on `WebGPURenderer` |
| `WorldImage` | Image plane in world space, 1 unit tall and as wide as the image aspect, optionally screen aligned (`screen_aligned`, sized by `size`), with `opacity`. Call `update_texture()` after the image changes. Runs on `WebGPURenderer` |
| `UpdatableMaterialMesh` | Mesh with dynamically-updated material: calls `material.update()` before each draw, if the material has one |

See `docs/Components.md` for the full API.

### View & Transition System

| Class | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ViewManager` | Manages application views/screens: `go_to_view(name, change_url?, skip?)`, `get`, `get_by_url`; keeps the URL and title in sync |
| `ViewComponent` | Base class for UI view components, shown and hidden by its `<name>_opacity` state key |
| `ViewComponentManager` | Manages view component lifecycle; updates the visible components each frame |
| `ApplicationView` | Base class for application views; registers itself and its enter transition data, sets its opacity from `<name>_opacity` |
| `TransitionManager` | Manages animated transitions between states; owns the state data (`current_state_data`, `set_default_state_data`) |
| `TransitionTable` | Holds each view's transition data and builds the `ActionSequencer` for a transition (exact `from`/`to` entry first, else the one with only `to`) |
| `ActionSequencer` | Timeline over a context object: one channel of keyframes per key (`add_action_interpolator`), plus `ActionEvent`s at set times; `update(dt)` writes the values |
| `NumberInterpolator` / `VectorInterpolator` | Keyframe interpolators extending `ActionInterpolator`, eased by an `EasingFunctions` name. Only `NumberInterpolator` has the `evaluate()` the sequencer calls |
| `ActionEvent` | Calls `window.ViewApi.application[name][method](...args.split(','))` when the sequencer passes its time |
| `ActionSequencerBuilder` / `DrawIOAnimationSheet` | Build an `ActionSequencer` from transition data (adding tracks that return untouched keys to their defaults) or from a draw.io timeline |

### Primitives

Ready-to-use 3D primitives: `Arrow`, `Cube`, `Sphere`, `HorizontalPlane`, `VerticalPlane`.

### Utilities

| Utility | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `OMath` | Extended math functions (lerp, clamp, `linear_map`, pingpong, angles, centroid, `matrix4_lerp`, random color, UUID) |
| `EasingFunctions` | Standard easing curves for animation. Their names are the easing strings in transition data |
| `CameraUtilities` | Singleton instance. Frames points or a box for the camera's current rotation (`fit_points`, `fit_bounding_box_points`; `zoom` is a distance for perspective and `camera.zoom` for orthographic; it changes nothing), picks the point under the mouse on a plane, and projects world positions to canvas pixels |
| `PerspectiveFrustumPointFitter` / `OrthographicFrustumPointFitter` | Instantiated. The framing math: the closest camera position that sees every point, and view bounds, zoom and near/far depth fitting for orthographic cameras |
| `FrustumPointFitter` | Instantiated. An older, unused copy of `PerspectiveFrustumPointFitter` that logs to the console on every fit |
| `GeometryUtilities` | Non-indexed copy of a geometry with a `barycentric` attribute (used by `Grid`) |
| `MeshSampler` | Random point sampling on mesh surfaces, area weighted, with normals, tangents and UVs. Indexed geometry only |
| `ModelUtilities` | GLTF model processing helpers: find objects, assign materials, shadow flags, clone a skinned GLTF |
| `ArrayUtilities` | Array manipulation helpers (in place) |
| `StringUtilities` | String helpers (capitalize, snake to camelCase, random color) |
| `TimeUtilities` | Parses `'hh:mm:ss'` time strings into milliseconds (`time_str_to_ms`, an instance method) |
| `ImageUtilities` | Reads an image's pixels on the CPU (`get_image_data`, `get_pixel`) |
| `HTMLUtilities` | Lazy loading: copies `data-src` into `src` inside a container |
| `ObjectUtilities` | Object helpers (`merge_deep`, `xml_to_json`) |
| `Validation` | Number and JSON checks (`is_int`, `is_float`, `is_number`, `is_json`) |
| `CSSAnimator` | Tweens one CSS property with an easing; call `update()` every frame. Ends when the eased value reaches 1, so some easings end early or never |

`CameraUtilities`, `MeshSampler` and `ModelUtilities` are singleton instances, `TimeUtilities`, `CSSAnimator` and the three frustum point fitters are instantiated, and the rest only have static methods.

### Camera Controller

`CameraController` is an orbital rig: a target (`reference_position`), a rotation from tilt and orientation in degrees, and a distance (`reference_zoom`). Each `update()` (called by the scene, not automatically) runs the current state (`AbstractCameraState` idle, or a `CommonCameraState` subclass that reads WASD, wheel and mouse drags), then the movement mode (`CameraMovementMode`; the default `ImmediateMode` places the camera on the same frame). It also frames points, boxes and spheres for perspective and orthographic cameras.

| Class | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `CameraController` | Rotation, translation, zoom and framing; swaps states (`set_state`) and modes (`set_mode`) |
| `CameraMovementMode` / `ImmediateMode` | Turns the reference values into the camera transform |
| `AbstractCameraState` / `CommonCameraState` | Reacts to input each frame and edits the reference values |

## Source Directory Structure

```
src/
  index.ts                    Main entry point (re-exports everything)
  BaseApplication.ts          Base class users extend
  RenderLoop.ts               Frame loop driver
  Graphics.ts                 Renderer wrapper (singleton)
  Time.ts                     Timing system (singleton)
  OScreen.ts                  Screen metrics (singleton)
  SceneManager.ts             Scene management (singleton)
  CameraManager.ts            Camera access (singleton)
  Initializer.ts              Bootstrap/teardown (singleton)
  Debug.ts                    Debug visualization (singleton)
  ResourceContainer.ts        Asset cache (singleton)
  OS.ts                       Platform detection (singleton)
  Browser.ts                  Browser detection
  Capabilities.ts             GPU capabilities
  KeyboardInput.ts            Keyboard state tracking
  PerspectiveCamera.ts        Extended Three.js PerspectiveCamera
  OrthographicCamera.ts       Extended Three.js OrthographicCamera
  Screen.ts                   Screen utilities
  action_sequencer/           Event sequencing and interpolators
  camera_controller/          Camera controller with movement modes
  canvas_drawer/              Canvas 2D drawing utilities
  components/                 Renderable components (Grid, Text2D, SDF, etc.)
  data_textures/              Data texture utilities
  html_utilities/             CSS animation helpers
  lib/                        Internal library code
  loaders/                    Async batch loaders
  materials/                  TSL node materials
  primitives/                 Geometric primitives
  raycast/                    Ray intersection utilities
  render_mode/                Rendering strategies
  render_utilities/           Post-processing (blur, depth, blit)
  resource_loader/            17 exported asset loaders (DDSLoader, SVGLoader unexported)
  scenes/                     AbstractScene and loading states
  shaders/                    Shared TSL shader nodes (grid)
  utilities/                  Math, easing, geometry, camera helpers
  view_components/            View/UI layer with transitions
```

## Build System

- **Bundler:** Rollup
- **Output:** `build/index.mjs` (ES module with sourcemaps, minified with terser)
- **Types:** `types/index.d.ts` (generated from `src/` by `yarn generate-types`)
- **Externals:** `three` and its sub-modules are not bundled

## Commands

```bash
yarn start            # Development watch mode
yarn build            # Production build
yarn generate-types   # Generate TypeScript declarations
yarn fix-syntax       # Lint and auto-fix with ESLint
yarn upload           # Build, publish to npm, and create git tag
```

## Key Design Patterns

1. **Singletons everywhere** — Core services are instantiated at module level and exported. Access them directly: `Time.delta_time`, `Graphics.render()`, `OScreen.width`, etc.
2. **Lifecycle hooks** — Extend `BaseApplication` and override only the hooks you need. The framework calls them in the correct order.
3. **Render mode swapping** — Change the entire rendering pipeline at runtime via `Graphics.set_state(new UnrealBloomRender())`.
4. **Two-phase asset loading** — Regular assets load first (with compilators spreading GPU work across frames), then high-quality assets load in the background.
5. **Fixed timestep** — Physics and deterministic logic runs in `fixed_update()` at 1/30s, with `frame_interpolation` available for smooth visual interpolation.
6. **State machine application** — `RenderLoop.set_state()` swaps the active `BaseApplication` instance FSM-style, calling `on_exit`/`on_enter`.
